title: Brouwer Degree via Mathlib Homology: the Functorial Core
description: The algebraic and functorial core of Brouwer degree theory, instantiated on Mathlib's genuine singular-homology functor (AlgebraicTopology.singularHomologyFunctor, Andrew Yang 2025). For a self-map f : X → X the degree is the integer by which the induced endomorphism acts on Hₙ(X) after the identification Hₙ(X) ≅ ℤ. We prove, with 0 sorries and 0 axioms: deg(id)=1, multiplicativity deg(g∘f)=deg(g)·deg(f), independence of the chosen identification Hₙ(X)≅ℤ, and that a homeomorphism has degree ±1. The identification Hₙ(Sⁿ)≅ℤ — which Mathlib's homology theory cannot yet provide (it currently computes only homology of totally disconnected spaces) — enters as an explicit hypothesis, never an axiom, so the results have the honest shape 'given the standard identification Hₙ(X)≅ℤ, the degree is well defined and functorial'.

meta.author: Formalized in Lean 4 (Mathlib)
assumptions: No axioms. The only foundational dependencies are the standard propext / Classical.choice / Quot.sound. The identification Hₙ(X) ≃+ ℤ is supplied as an explicit hypothesis on each statement, not as an axiom: theorems are conditional on this identification, which for X = Sⁿ is the mathematically standard Hₙ(Sⁿ) ≅ ℤ whose Lean proof awaits further Mathlib development (homotopy invariance / Eilenberg–Steenrod machinery).

mathlibDependencies.description: Mathlib's singular homology functor C ⥤ TopCat ⥤ C; specialized to coefficients ℤ in AddCommGrpCat it is Hₙ(-;ℤ) : TopCat ⥤ AddCommGrpCat
Functoriality F.map (f ≫ g) = F.map f ≫ F.map g — the source of degree multiplicativity
Turns a categorical isomorphism in AddCommGrpCat into an AddEquiv, used to obtain the automorphism for a homeomorphism's degree
ℤ-linearity of additive homomorphisms ℤ →+ ℤ; gives that any such map is multiplication by its value at 1
A unit of ℤ is ±1; converts 'degree of an automorphism is a unit' into 'degree is ±1'

originalContributions: degreeOfEnd: a clean definition of the degree of an endomorphism f : G →+ G of an abelian group through a chosen identification e : G ≃+ ℤ, as the integer e(f(e⁻¹ 1))
degreeOfEnd_conj: the conjugate of f to ℤ is exactly multiplication by the degree — the characterizing property, proved by exhibiting the conjugate as an AddMonoidHom ℤ →+ ℤ and using ℤ-linearity
degreeOfEnd_comp: multiplicativity / functoriality deg(g∘f)=deg(g)·deg(f), the algebraic heart of degree theory
degreeOfEnd_indep: the degree is independent of the chosen identification Hₙ ≅ ℤ — the well-definedness theorem, proved via ℤ-linearity of the change-of-identification automorphism
degreeOfEnd_equiv_eq: an automorphism has degree exactly +1 or -1 (degree is a unit of ℤ, hence ±1)

functorDegree + functorDegree_id / functorDegree_comp / functorDegree_iso_eq: the degree transported through an arbitrary functor F : C ⥤ AddCommGrpCat, deriving id↦1 and multiplicativity directly from the functor laws map_id / map_comp

brouwerDegree: the above instantiated on Mathlib's genuine singularHomologyFunctor with ℤ coefficients, with brouwerDegree_id, brouwerDegree_comp, and brouwerDegree_iso_eq (homeomorphisms have degree ±1), plus a ContinuousMap convenience wrapper brouwerDegreeCM

overview.historicalContext:
**The Brouwer degree.** For a continuous self-map f : Sⁿ → Sⁿ, the Brouwer degree deg(f) is the integer by which the induced map f∗ on the top homology Hₙ(Sⁿ) ≅ ℤ acts. It is the cornerstone invariant of algebraic topology: it powers the hairy-ball theorem, the fundamental theorem of algebra, the Borsuk–Ulam theorem (via the antipodal degree (-1)ⁿ⁺¹), and the Lefschetz and Hopf index theorems. Classically (Brouwer 1911) the degree was defined geometrically; the homological definition (Eilenberg–Steenrod) makes its two defining properties — deg(id)=1 and multiplicativity under composition — into immediate consequences of homology being a functor.

Mathlib gained a genuine singular homology theory only in 2025 (Andrew Yang). It defines the singular chain complex and homology functor for arbitrary coefficients, but so far computes homology only for totally disconnected spaces; the computation Hₙ(Sⁿ) ≅ ℤ, and the homotopy-invariance / Eilenberg–Steenrod machinery needed to obtain it, are not yet available. This entry isolates the purely formal content of the degree — everything that follows from functoriality plus Hₙ(Sⁿ)≅ℤ — and proves it in full, instantiated on Mathlib's actual homology functor, with the identification Hₙ(X)≅ℤ kept as an explicit hypothesis rather than an axiom.
overview.keyInsight: The two headline properties of the Brouwer degree — deg(id)=1 and deg(g∘f)=deg(g)·deg(f) — are not analytic facts but a restatement of the functor laws F.map(id)=id and F.map(f≫g)=F.map(f)≫F.map(g) for the homology functor F, read through the identification End(Hₙ)≅End(ℤ)≅ℤ. Likewise 'a homeomorphism has degree ±1' is just 'an automorphism of ℤ is ±1', and 'the degree is well defined' is the ℤ-linearity (centrality of multiplication) that makes the choice of identification Hₙ≅ℤ irrelevant. Separating this formal core from the missing analytic input (Hₙ(Sⁿ)≅ℤ) yields a fully verified, axiom-free contribution and pinpoints exactly what remains for Mathlib to deliver.
overview.problemStatement: Define the Brouwer degree of a continuous self-map via Mathlib's genuine singular-homology functor and prove its defining properties — deg(id)=1, multiplicativity deg(g∘f)=deg(g)·deg(f), independence of the identification Hₙ(X)≅ℤ, and degree ±1 for homeomorphisms — with the identification Hₙ(X)≃+ℤ held as an explicit hypothesis rather than an axiom.
overview.proofStrategy: Work in three layers. (I) Algebraic core: for an abelian group G with a chosen e : G ≃+ ℤ, define degreeOfEnd e f = e(f(e⁻¹ 1)) and prove the conjugation identity (the conjugate of f to ℤ is multiplication by the degree) via ℤ-linearity; everything else — identity, multiplicativity, identification-independence, ±1 for automorphisms — follows from this one lemma. (II) Functorial layer: transport the degree through an arbitrary functor F : C ⥤ AddCommGrpCat so that the degree's identity and multiplicativity become the functor laws map_id and map_comp. (III) Instantiation: feed Mathlib's singular-homology functor Hₙ(-;ℤ) into layer II to obtain the genuine Brouwer degree, with all properties inherited verbatim.
keyInsights: **Degree = functor laws.** deg(id)=1 and deg(g∘f)=deg(g)·deg(f) are not analytic facts about spheres; they are exactly F.map_id and F.map_comp for the homology functor F, read through End(Hₙ)≅End(ℤ)≅ℤ.

**One lemma does the work.** The conjugation identity e(f(e⁻¹ n)) = deg(f)·n — proved purely from ℤ-linearity of additive maps ℤ→+ℤ — is the single fact from which identity, multiplicativity, well-definedness, and the ±1 law all follow.

**Well-definedness is centrality of scalars.** Independence of the chosen identification Hₙ≅ℤ is the statement that the change-of-identification automorphism ψ : ℤ→+ℤ, being ℤ-linear, leaves the scalar fixed — i.e. integer multiplication is conjugation-invariant.
**±1 is a unit fact.** 'A homeomorphism has degree ±1' is just 'an automorphism of ℤ is a unit, and the units of ℤ are ±1' (Int.isUnit_iff), with no topology involved.

**Honest boundary.** Keeping Hₙ(X)≃+ℤ as a hypothesis rather than an axiom makes every theorem an explicit conditional and pinpoints the exact analytic input (homotopy invariance / Eilenberg–Steenrod, yielding Hₙ(Sⁿ)≅ℤ) that Mathlib still owes.

sections.title: Overview: scope and the honest hypothesis
sections.summary: States what is proved (the functorial core of Brouwer degree on Mathlib's real homology functor) and what is assumed (Hₙ(X) ≅ ℤ, as a hypothesis not an axiom). Explains why the analytic computation Hₙ(Sⁿ)≅ℤ is the remaining Mathlib gap.
sections.mathContext: Mathlib's singular homology currently computes only homology of totally disconnected spaces; Hₙ(Sⁿ)≅ℤ requires homotopy invariance / Eilenberg–Steenrod axioms not yet formalized.

sections.title: Section I.a — degreeOfEnd: conjugation, identity, multiplicativity, independence
sections.summary: degreeOfEnd is defined and its well-definedness cluster is proved: the conjugation characterization (degreeOfEnd_conj) — the single lemma everything else rests on — identity (degreeOfEnd_id), multiplicativity (degreeOfEnd_comp), and independence of the chosen identification e (degreeOfEnd_indep).
sections.mathContext: An additive map ℤ→+ℤ is multiplication by its value at 1 (AddMonoidHom.map_zsmul); this ℤ-linearity is what makes deg(f) well defined independently of the chosen e : G ≃+ ℤ.

sections.title: Section I.b — Automorphisms have degree ±1
sections.summary: degreeOfEnd_equiv_isUnit: the degree of an automorphism σ : G ≃+ G is a unit of ℤ, via degreeOfEnd_comp applied to σ and σ⁻¹. degreeOfEnd_equiv_eq: units of ℤ are exactly ±1 (Int.isUnit_iff), giving the sharp dichotomy deg(σ) = 1 ∨ deg(σ) = -1.
sections.mathContext: IsUnit.of_mul_eq_one from σ.comp σ.symm = id; Int.isUnit_iff : IsUnit (n:ℤ) ↔ n = 1 ∨ n = -1.

sections.title: Section II — Functorial degree through a functor to abelian groups
sections.summary: functorDegree transports the degree through any F : C ⥤ AddCommGrpCat; functorDegree_id and functorDegree_comp derive the identity and multiplicativity directly from the functor laws, and functorDegree_iso_eq gives degree ±1 for isomorphisms.
sections.mathContext: Homology is a functor; the degree's defining properties are the functor laws read through End(Hₙ)≅ℤ.

sections.title: Section III — Instantiation on Mathlib's singular homology
sections.summary: Hn n is Mathlib's Hₙ(-;ℤ) : TopCat ⥤ AddCommGrpCat; brouwerDegree, brouwerDegree_id, brouwerDegree_comp, brouwerDegree_iso_eq, and the ContinuousMap wrappers brouwerDegreeCM / brouwerDegreeCM_id give the Brouwer degree of continuous self-maps via genuine Mathlib homology.
sections.mathContext: singularHomologyFunctor AddCommGrpCat n applied to ℤ is the n-th integral singular homology functor; degree is defined for any space whose n-th homology is identified with ℤ.

conclusion.summary: This entry delivers the complete functorial core of Brouwer degree theory — definition, conjugation characterization, identity, multiplicativity, identification-independence, and the ±1 degree of a homeomorphism — fully machine-verified (0 sorries, 0 axioms) and instantiated on Mathlib's genuine singular-homology functor. The single mathematical input it does not supply, Hₙ(Sⁿ)≅ℤ, is held as an explicit hypothesis rather than smuggled in as an axiom, faithfully marking the boundary of what Mathlib's homology can currently prove. The remaining work toward a fully unconditional Lean Brouwer degree is precisely the homotopy invariance and Eilenberg–Steenrod computation that yields Hₙ(Sⁿ)≅ℤ.
conclusion.implications: By factoring the degree into a reusable algebraic layer (degreeOfEnd on any G ≃+ ℤ) and a functorial layer (functorDegree through any F : C ⥤ AddCommGrpCat), the development becomes a drop-in foundation: the day Mathlib proves Hₙ(Sⁿ)≅ℤ, the hypothesis e instantiates and the Brouwer degree of every continuous self-map of a sphere becomes unconditional, immediately yielding the antipodal degree (-1)ⁿ⁺¹ and hence the homological Borsuk–Ulam theorem, the hairy-ball theorem, and a topological proof of the fundamental theorem of algebra. The same functorial degree works for any space with a known top homology, not just spheres.
openQuestions: Supply the missing analytic input Hₙ(Sⁿ)≅ℤ in Mathlib via homotopy invariance and the Eilenberg–Steenrod / Mayer–Vietoris machinery, discharging the hypothesis e and making brouwerDegree unconditional for spheres.
Derive the antipodal-map degree deg(a) = (-1)ⁿ⁺¹ and use it to formalize the homological proof of Borsuk–Ulam (the parent OQ), replacing its Borsuk–Ulam axiom with the degree computation.
Establish homotopy invariance of the degree (homotopic maps have equal degree) so that the degree descends to [Sⁿ, Sⁿ], recovering the classical isomorphism deg : πₙ(Sⁿ) ≅ ℤ.
